_comment: Single source of truth for the app's version, both stores.
It lives here rather than under android-config/ because iOS and Android
drifted apart while they had separate sources: Android reached 5.2 while
the iOS Info.plist still said 4.1.0, so the same release described itself
two different ways.
versionName is the user-visible marketing version. Android reads it as
versionName, iOS as CFBundleShortVersionString.
androidVersionCode: Play requires it to be strictly higher than anything
already uploaded to the track. Only Play knows what has been used, so no
local check can verify it — bump it for every upload and never reuse one.
iosBuildNumber: CFBundleVersion. Two App Store Connect rules apply. A
marketing version whose build was approved for sale is a CLOSED train and
rejects any further upload at any build number (error 90186) — 4.0.9 is
closed for that reason. Within an open train, CFBundleVersion must strictly
increase (error 90062). Build numbers ran 79, 83, 84, 85, were then reset
to 4-7 for 4.0.9, and are now kept monotonic ACROSS trains so that 'what is
the next build number' has one unambiguous answer.
Moving versionName to 5.2 opens a new iOS train and abandons 4.1.0.
Anything already uploaded under 4.1.0 stays there and cannot be promoted.
The two numbers are kept equal deliberately: nothing requires it, but it
makes a build identifiable across both stores from one figure.
Run `npm run apply:android` / `npm run apply:ios` after changing this.
